To measure these quantities accurately the frequency counter must be set up correctly.
In this lesson, you will correctly set up a frequency counter to measure an AC sine wave.
The Nida Model 410 Multifunction Counter is used in this lesson.
If you are using a different model, the procedures are still valid. Most frequency counters are identical in operation, but the location and names of the controls may be different.
Let's begin the lesson on FREQUENCY COUNTER USE.
. The experiment in this lesson is not setup to use the selected trainer.
LESSON MENU

This experiment demonstrates the operation of frequency counters. You will correctly set up a frequency counter and perform the check function, measure period, frequency, and total pulses using a function generator and experiment card
EXPERIMENT
Pick up the PC130-10 card. This card contains a series resistance circuit used to measure signals. The card uses both DC and AC inputs.
The function generator is used to produce an AC signal applied to pin E.
This signal is directly connected to TP2 on the experiment card.
S1 selects between positive or negative DC voltage. It will not be used in this experiment.

2. Carefully plug PC130-10 into the Test Console PC1 position.

Gate - .1 sec Range - 1 k Function - sine wave Modulation - Out

7. Press the RESET switch on the frequency counter and hold it in. Notice the display is blank. As soon as you release this switch, it will begin incrementing from zero. 8. Release the RESET switch and observe the process.
MULTIFUNCTION COUNTER SETUP - Set the Frequency Counter to Reset.

9. Press the HOLD switch on the frequency counter. Notice the display is held at the number of cycles received up until the time you pressed HOLD. However, only the display is stopped. The circuits inside the frequency counter are still counting cycles.
MULTIFUNCTION COUNTER SETUP - Set the Frequency Counter Display to Hold.

10. Press the HOLD switch again. Notice the display immediately resumes at the actual number of pulses received since the last time the RESET switch was pressed. The counting process does not stop when the HOLD button is pressed.
11. Press the RESET switch in and hold it in.
12. Press the 1 M range switch on the function generator. 13. Ensure that the frequency dial on the function generator is set to 5.
MULTIFUNCTION COUNTER SETUP - Set the Frequency Counter Display to Reset.
MEASUREMENT SETUP - Change Function Generator Range to 1 M and turn Frequency Dial to 5.
The function generator is producing a 5 MHz signal. When you release the RESET switch, the frequency counter display will begin incrementing at a rate of 5 million times per second. i

14. Release the RESET switch and observe the process.
